surfaces.part: rubble block pile (stacked stone blocks, stepped silhouette)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a stepped pile that widens from 11px at rows 9-10 to 44px at rows 22-28. Every column scan shows alternating light block faces (L~190-210) and dark outline or mortar rows (#3a2b55, #975575), which looks like a grid of front-facing block faces. No row has a front-edge line followed by eave shadow, no ellipse is present, and no horizontal surface is visible. The top rows 9-10 are only a dark purple outline. The grass at rows 29-31 is a base decoration. For a debris object this is a flat front view of stacked blocks with no top planes.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a rubble heap of individually shaded stones and brick chunks, with light, mid and dark pink-grey tones, highlight dots and darker gaps between pieces. I count about 5 lightness steps on the stone material, in line with the references. Measured facts support this: 34 visible tones per tile against 17-20 for the stall and well, 0% near-flat coverage, and only 2% neutral dark edge pixels. The edges lean toward a tinted dark rose-brown rather than a black sticker line. A rubble pile is a reasonable standing prop next to the stall and well. It is somewhat messy at 2x, but nothing reads as flat or thin.

surfaces.part: rubble heap of stacked stone blocks (main mass)

answer.evidence: The pile is a stepped silhouette (widths 11, 20, 29, 35, then 44) built from face-on block faces with dark purple outlines. Rows 9-10 (width 11) are only an outline-like cap on the highest block. No band with a front-edge line and eave shadow, no ellipse, and no visible contents. The step edges at rows 11, 15 and 22 do not read as horizontal surfaces. The mass is a front view of stacked blocks (rows 11-30) with no horizontal top planes.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a pile of rubble stones with small plant tufts. Its measured 34 visible tones per 16x16 tile are well above prop-well-roofed (20), prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Only 2% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean toward the tint of the neighbouring stone and vegetation rather than a black sticker line. By eye, the stones are shaded one by one with light and dark clumps and speckle, which matches Beodeul's per-stone shading. I estimate about 5 lightness steps on the stone ramp, close to the references' 5-6. The image is small and the detail is hard to confirm, but the measurements and the visible clustering support a pass.

answer.evidence: The object is a stepped pile of pink-grey stone blocks with dark outlines, widening from 11 px at rows 9-10 to 44 px at rows 22-28. Each tier is drawn as front-facing block faces: pale block faces sit between dark mortar lines, and the dark rows at x=24 (13, 20, 23-24) are joints, not eave shadow. There is no single front-edge line, no ellipse, and no visible contents of a container. The top rows 9-10 are only the outline and one row of block, about 2 rows, so this is a rim at most. The silhouette is a tiered heap seen face-on, so it reads as front elevation rather than a 3/4 volume. Green grass sits at the bottom (rows 29-31).

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a low rubble pile of pinkish stones with pale highlights. It reads as a prop of the same kind as the references. Measured facts: 34 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above the well (20) and cheese stall (17). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Only 2% of dark edge pixels are neutral, which means the dark edges lean toward the material tone rather than a black sticker line. By eye, individual stones and chunks are shaded one by one, with highlights, mid tones and dark gaps, about 5 steps. This matches the per-stone shading of the references. The piece sits within the range of the references in density and shading, and a careful artist would accept it next to them.

surfaces.part: top brick cluster of the pile

answer.evidence: The rubble is a stepped heap of brick and plaster blocks, and each block is drawn face-on with dark outlines. The silhouette steps outward from width 11 at rows 9-10 to 20 at rows 11-14, 35 at rows 16-21 and about 44 at rows 22-28. The steps are only 1-2 row ledges. None of them has a front-edge line followed by eave shadow, and there is no ellipse or sloped plane. The columns at x=24 and x=35 alternate light block faces with dark outline rows (rows 13, 17, 20, 23-24). That pattern reads as vertical brick faces, not horizontal tops. The pale highlights at rows 11-16 are brick faces or rims. The stepped silhouette gives a mound outline, but no clear foreshortened top plane is visible. The pile reads as a front elevation of stacked blocks.
